audit_findings.title: Management’s “growth” capex includes economically sustaining work
audit_findings.magnitude: $347.7 million 2025 growth-capex pool; sustaining subset unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Economically sustaining reconfiguration spending belongs in the maintenance-capex deduction from OE; understating that deduction inflates 2025 OE, the fitted anchor and every scenario.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition to newly–acquired compressors, growth capital expenditures include the upgrading of major components on an existing compression package where the current configuration of the compression package is no longer in demand and the compressor is not likely to return to an operating status without the capital expenditures.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that management’s growth-capex category is not purely expansionary, but it does not demonstrate how much of the $347.7 million was required to keep existing packages commercially deployable or whether the OE ledger independently reclassified it. The disclosed pool is 136.8% of the $254.1 million anchor, so the unresolved sustaining portion is reasonably capable of materially changing intrinsic value.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the 2025 project-level growth-capex ledger, identify upgrades to existing packages, reconcile them to idle-fleet redeployments, retirements, disposals and depreciation, and rerun OE and all scenarios using economic maintenance capex.

audit_findings.title: The earnings anchor and current equity claim span different operating perimeters
audit_findings.mechanism: The current-perimeter OE anchor must include a full year of the businesses now owned, exclude disposed operations, incorporate the current financing and tax burden, and be divided by the corresponding fully diluted shares.
audit_findings.evidence: The results of operations attributable to the NGCS Acquisition have been included in our consolidated financial statements as part of our contract operations segment since the NGCS acquisition date.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated: NGCS entered reported results only from May 1, 2025, while acquisition shares and financing are in the current claim; historical observations also cross the TOPS acquisition and Flowco disposition. NGCS’s filed 2025 pro forma information adds $26.277 million of revenue and $7.789 million of net income relative to reported results, but it does not provide OE, and the offsetting Flowco and financing effects are not established. Because the $254.1 million anchor is derived from incomparable perimeters, the valuation impact is unresolved but reasonably capable of being material.
audit_findings.action: Construct a current-perimeter pro forma OE with full-year NGCS and TOPS, no Flowco operations, current debt interest, taxes and economic maintenance, pair it with 177.889 million fully diluted shares, and rerun the scenarios.

audit_findings.title: A nonrecurring tax-audit benefit is buried in operating costs
audit_findings.magnitude: $35.8 million pretax; approximately $27.3 million after the filed 23.8% 2025 effective tax rate; approximately $5.8 million maximum reduction to the fitted anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: If unadjusted, the benefit raises 2025 OE and, through the final observation’s approximately 34.5% weight in the ten-year log-trend endpoint, raises the anchor and scenario values.
audit_findings.evidence: We settled certain sales and use tax audits for which we recorded a net benefit of $ 27.8 million during the year ended December 31, 2025, which is primarily reflected as a decrease to cost of sales, exclusive of depreciation and amortization.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the OE ledger removed the benefit remains unresolved, but its maximum effect can be bounded. Removing approximately $27.3 million after tax from 2025 OE would reduce the fitted anchor from $254.1 million to about $248.3 million, or 2.3%. Scenario values would fall by roughly $0.39 to $0.54 per share; even the bull value would remain about $23.24 versus the $32.69 market price. It therefore cannot change the present valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the OE adjustment ledger for removal of the full $27.8 million settlement and $8.0 million credit, verify consistent treatment of the $41.5 million receivable and related liabilities, and correct the series if absent.

audit_findings.title: Enerflex capital calls can bypass owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.123 million paid in 2025; future obligations unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Capital calls recorded directly in financing activities and equity bypass OE; expected future calls must therefore reduce future OE or be deducted in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The separation and distribution agreement specifies our right to receive payments from Enerflex and our obligation to satisfy capital calls from Enerflex
audit_findings.explanation: The $1.123 million 2025 leakage is demonstrated and by itself equals only about $0.006 per diluted share and 0.03%-0.04% of scenario equity value. However, the separation agreement creates a continuing obligation whose triggers, limits and duration are absent from the record. Future value impact is therefore unresolved and cannot be shown either material or immaterial.
audit_findings.action: Review the separation and distribution agreement and subsequent Enerflex notices for call triggers, caps, duration, outstanding claims and expected payments; then deduct the probability-weighted obligation from OE or the equity bridge.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition costs may have been retained as recurring expense
audit_findings.magnitude: $25.954 million pretax across 2024-2025; approximately $19.5 million after the filed annual effective tax rates; approximately $4.6 million maximum increase to the fitted anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Deal-specific costs retained in historical OE depress the 2024 and 2025 observations and therefore the fitted anchor; any recurring acquisition allowance would reduce the permissible add-back.
audit_findings.evidence: We incurred $ 9.1 million of professional fees, compensation and other costs related to the NGCS Acquisition during the year ended December 31, 2025, and we incurred $ 3.6 million and $ 13.2 million of professional fees, compensation and other costs related to the TOPS Acquisition during the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate $13.249 million of 2024 and $12.705 million of 2025 transaction costs, but the adjustment ledger does not establish whether they remained in OE. Even assuming all were retained and fully added back after tax, the fitted anchor would rise only about 1.8%, producing roughly $0.31-$0.43 per share of scenario value. The bull value would remain near $24.20 versus the $32.69 market price, so this cannot change the valuation conclusion; retaining a recurring inorganic-growth allowance would make the effect smaller.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the OE adjustment ledger, identify transaction-specific versus recurring acquisition costs, and document any normalization; rerun the trend only if the ledger did not already make the adjustment.
